simple: an error that happens while the kernel runs and is reported by a later call.
analogy: a helper dropping a jar in the far pantry; you hear about it the next time you talk to the hall.
precise: because a launch returns before the kernel ends, errors inside the kernel (such as cudaErrorIllegalAddress) are returned by a later synchronizing or other runtime call.
source: D1 of F6-05 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the program that runs your kernels, times them by the protocol, checks the answers and prints the table.
analogy: the quality desk's stopwatch, logbook and rules, the same for every order.
precise: E1's "benchmark harness (timing, correctness checks, result tables)", "in C++ with a common interface for CUDA and HIP back ends"; this course's project.
source: C1 of F6-06 (Systems Curriculum (this project), milestone E1 (goal and build quoted) and section 13.4 (measurement protocol quoted verbatim). A map, not a source (AH-4))

simple: not just close, but the very same bits in every result.
analogy: Kwame's scale shows identical weights to the last digit.
precise: two floating-point results are bit-exact when their encodings are identical (compared as 32-bit integers, as Listing 2 does); stronger than "within a tolerance".
source: C1 of F6-04 (Systems Curriculum (this project), milestone E1 (acceptance test quoted verbatim) and section 13.4 ("Correctness first: compare against a CPU reference or the v)

simple: which table you sit at, and how many seats each table has in each direction.
analogy: table (2, 1); tables of 16 × 16 seats.
precise: built-in variables holding the block's coordinates within the grid and the block's dimensions in threads; all blocks of one launch have the same dimensions.
source: D1 of F6-02 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the threads of a warp reading neighbouring addresses, so the hardware can serve them with few, full memory transfers.
analogy: the row needs neighbouring jars, fetched in one trip per section.
precise: the device combines the global loads or stores of a warp's threads into as few memory transactions as their addresses allow (paraphrase; the exact rules are in D1); efficiency is the ratio of bytes requested to bytes moved.
source: D1 of F6-08 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Best Practices Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a tool that runs your program and watches every memory access and synchronisation of every GPU thread.
analogy: an inspector who follows every helper and notes each reach into the wrong shelf.
precise: NVIDIA's correctness tool compute-sanitizer with sub-tools memcheck (memory access checking, the default), racecheck, synccheck and initcheck, as listed by its own help.
source: R5 of F6-05 (compute-sanitizer --help excerpt (sanitizer_help.log), version 2022.4.1)

simple: a small read-only area for values that are the same for every thread.
analogy: the menu board on the wall.
precise: device memory declared __constant__, read-only for kernels, written from the host with cudaMemcpyToSymbol, accessed through a cache; its total size is the device property totalConstMem.
source: D1 of F6-03 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide"); H1 of F6-03 (CUDA 12.0 header driver_types.h as installed (Ubuntu package nvidia-cuda-dev 12.0.146~12.0.1-4build4), read in this build: cudaDeviceProp fields totalConstMem, ) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the compiler merging a multiply and an add written separately into one FMA.
analogy: the hall replacing "measure, level, add, level" by its one-pour cup without asking.
precise: nvcc's help: --fmad "enables (disables) the contraction of floating-point multiplies and adds/subtracts into floating-point multiply-add operations (FMAD, FFMA, or DFMA)".
source: R5 of F6-04 (nvcc's help text recorded in this build (university/labs/F6-01/nvcc_help.log), including --fmad and its default)

simple: a plain CPU version of the computation whose answers you trust and compare against.
analogy: the head chef's own version of the dish at the quality desk.
precise: an independent implementation (often the obvious loop) used as the test oracle; curriculum 13.4: "compare against a CPU reference or the vendor library with a tolerance justified by the precision".
source: C1 of F6-04 (Systems Curriculum (this project), milestone E1 (acceptance test quoted verbatim) and section 13.4 ("Correctness first: compare against a CPU reference or the v)

simple: a marker you put into the GPU's queue of work; the GPU notes the time when it reaches it.
analogy: a slip in the order queue saying "stamp the clock when you get here".
precise: a cudaEvent_t recorded with cudaEventRecord; cudaEventElapsedTime "Computes the elapsed time between two events (in milliseconds with a resolution of around 0.5 microseconds)".
source: H1 of F6-06 (CUDA 12.0 header cuda_runtime_api.h as installed (Ubuntu package nvidia-cuda-dev 12.0.146~12.0.1-4build4), read in this build and recorded in university/labs/F6) — installed header read in this build

simple: asking the runtime what GPU you have and what its limits are.
analogy: Nadia's walk through the hall with a notebook.
precise: cudaGetDeviceCount and cudaGetDeviceProperties, which fill a cudaDeviceProp structure; NVIDIA's deviceQuery sample prints the same structure.
source: H1 of F6-07 (CUDA 12.0 headers as installed (Ubuntu package nvidia-cuda-dev 12.0.146~12.0.1-4build4), read in this build: driver_types.h (struct cudaDeviceProp field comment); D2 of F6-07 (NVIDIA, "CUDA Samples": deviceQuery; and "nvidia-smi" documentation) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a small box of three numbers (x, y, z) used to give the size of a grid or a block.
analogy: "63 across, 38 down, 1 high" written on the order slip.
precise: a CUDA struct with members x, y, z; the installed header's constructor gives every missing value the default 1, so dim3 block(16, 16) means 16 × 16 × 1.
source: H1 of F6-02 (CUDA 12.0 headers as installed (Ubuntu package nvidia-cuda-dev 12.0.146~12.0.1-4build4), read in this build: vector_types.h (struct dim3: members x, y, z, const) — installed header read in this build

simple: two numbers: the newest CUDA the installed driver supports, and the CUDA version your program was built with.
analogy: what the hall's door-keeper understands, and which edition of the recipe book you wrote from.
precise: both "(1000 × major + 10 × minor)"; the runtime version is, as of CUDA 12.0, "a compile-time constant stating the CUDA Toolkit version".
source: H1 of F6-07 (CUDA 12.0 headers as installed (Ubuntu package nvidia-cuda-dev 12.0.146~12.0.1-4build4), read in this build: driver_types.h (struct cudaDeviceProp field comment) — installed header read in this build

simple: how many bytes your kernel moved per second, counted from what it must read and write.
analogy: jars carried per minute by the whole hall.
precise: (bytes read + bytes written) ÷ time; in this course reported in GB/s with 1 GB = 10 bytes (bench::gbPerS); compared with the peak in F6-09.
source: F6-06 (this course's definition)

simple: the number every CUDA runtime function returns to say "it worked" or what went wrong.
analogy: the line the door-keeper writes in the logbook.
precise: an enumeration in driver_types.h; cudaSuccess means no error; each other value has a name (cudaGetErrorName) and a description (cudaGetErrorString).
source: H1 of F6-05 (CUDA 12.0 headers as installed (Ubuntu package nvidia-cuda-dev 12.0.146~12.0.1-4build4), read in this build: driver_types.h (comments of cudaErrorInvalidConfigu) — installed header read in this build

simple: the GPU part of your program, which can hold several versions of each kernel for different GPUs.
analogy: a folder of recipe cards printed for different kinds of hall.
precise: a container embedded in the executable holding machine code (cubin ELF) for real targets (sm_XX) and/or PTX for virtual targets (compute_XX); cuobjdump --list-elf and --list-ptx list them.
source: R4 of F6-07 (fatbinary of F6-04/saxpy.cu built for sm_90 only, listed with cuobjdump (fatbin_sm90.log), CUDA 12.0, compiled only); D3 of F6-07 (NVIDIA, "CUDA Compiler Driver NVCC") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the GPU's big main memory that every thread and the host (by copies) can reach.
analogy: the big pantry far away.
precise: device memory allocated with cudaMalloc (or declared __device__), visible to all threads of all launches and kept between launches until freed; accessed with ld.global/st.global in PTX.
source: D1 of F6-03 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide"); R1 of F6-03 (PTX of spaces for target sm_80, filtered to declarations, loads, stores and barriers (university/labs/F6-03/ptx_spaces.log), CUDA 12.0, compiled only) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: all the teams working on one job.
analogy: every table in the hall for this order.
precise: the set of all thread blocks created by one kernel launch.
source: D1 of F6-01 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how many tables there are in each direction.
analogy: 63 tables across, 38 down.
precise: a built-in variable holding the grid's dimensions in blocks, set by the first value of the execution configuration.
source: D1 of F6-02 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: each thread does element i, then jumps ahead by the total number of threads and does another, until the data runs out.
analogy: each helper takes every 8th tile when there are 8 helpers.
precise: a loop for (i = global index; i < n; i += blockDim.x * gridDim.x), which makes a kernel correct for any grid size.
source: D2 of F6-02 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Best Practices Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the host is the CPU side of your program; the device is the GPU.
analogy: Amara's kitchen (host) and the hall of helpers (device), each with its own pantry.
precise: in CUDA the host is the CPU and its memory, which runs ordinary C++ and starts work on the device; the device is the GPU and its own memory, which runs kernels.
source: D1 of F6-01 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide"); D3 of F6-01 (Wen-mei Hwu, David Kirk, Izzat El Hajj, "Programming Massively Parallel Processors: A Hands-on Approach") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a launch refused before any thread runs, for example because the block is too big.
analogy: the door-keeper refusing an impossible table size.
precise: such as cudaErrorInvalidConfiguration, which the header describes as "a kernel launch is requesting resources that can never be satisfied by the current device"; the launch syntax returns no value, so it is read with cudaGetLastError.
source: H1 of F6-05 (CUDA 12.0 headers as installed (Ubuntu package nvidia-cuda-dev 12.0.146~12.0.1-4build4), read in this build: driver_types.h (comments of cudaErrorInvalidConfigu) — installed header read in this build

simple: the moment the CPU tells the GPU "run this recipe with this many teams of this size".
analogy: Amara handing the order slip to the hall.
precise: a kernel call written kernel<<<blocks, threadsPerBlock>>>(arguments); the values between the triple angle brackets are the execution configuration.  Launches are asynchronous with respect to the host.
source: D1 of F6-01 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide"); H1 of F6-01 (CUDA 12.0 headers as installed in the build container (Ubuntu package nvidia-cuda-dev 12.0.146~12.0.1-4build4), read in this build: cuda_runtime_api.h (section ) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one number for a seat, counting across a table row first, then the next row.
analogy: seat numbers painted on the chairs, row by row.
precise: for a block of size (Dx, Dy), thread (x, y) has id x + y·Dx (and + z·Dx·Dy in 3-D); consecutive ids, in groups of 32, form the block's warps.
source: D1 of F6-02 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: what fraction of the bytes moved were actually wanted.
analogy: jars used ÷ jars carried.
precise: bytes requested by the warp ÷ (segments touched × segment size); Listing 1's last column. A profiler reports related ratios from hardware counters.
source: F6-08 (this course's definition)

simple: the smallest aligned block of bytes the memory system moves at a time.
analogy: a shelf section of eight jars, always fetched whole.
precise: in this course's TG-1 model, an aligned 32-byte unit; NVIDIA calls 32-byte units "sectors" and caches in 128-byte lines on many generations (from memory; check D1, D2).
source: D2 of F6-08 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one of the different places a GPU value can live, each with its own rules.
analogy: hands, table, menu board, pantry, private shelf.
precise: a class of memory with its own scope (which threads see it), lifetime and access instructions; PTX calls them state spaces and names them in its instructions (.reg, .shared, .global, .const, .local, .param).
source: D1 of F6-03 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide"); D4 of F6-03 (NVIDIA, "Parallel Thread Execution ISA" (state spaces) and "CUDA Binary Utilities" (SASS instruction set reference)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: ordinary host memory (malloc, new, std::vector), which the OS may move.
analogy: goods in the ordinary warehouse, carried to the dock first.
precise: for a cudaMemcpy from it to the device, the header says the function "will return once the pageable buffer has been copied to the staging memory for DMA transfer".
source: H1 of F6-09 (CUDA 12.0 header cuda_runtime_api.h as installed (Ubuntu package nvidia-cuda-dev 12.0.146~12.0.1-4build4), read in this build and recorded in university/labs/F6) — installed header read in this build

simple: each thread's own fastest storage for the values it is using right now.
analogy: each helper's hands.
precise: per-thread storage allocated by the compiler from the SM's register file for the thread's lifetime; ordinary local scalar variables live there; ptxas -v reports the count per thread.
source: D1 of F6-03 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide"); R2 of F6-03 (ptxas resource report for spaces (resources.log, -Xptxas -v, sm_80), CUDA 12.0) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: "times a, plus y": each element of y becomes a times the element of x, plus itself.
analogy: every helper multiplies a spoon of base by 1.7 and adds a spoon of stock.
precise: Single-precision A·X Plus Y, y[i] = a * x[i] + y[i] for float vectors x, y and scalar a; one of the classic BLAS level-1 operations.
source: D3 of F6-04 (Wen-mei Hwu, David Kirk, Izzat El Hajj, "Programming Massively Parallel Processors: A Hands-on Approach") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: an error after which the GPU cannot be used again in this process.
analogy: the hall is closed for the rest of the day; every new order comes back with the same note.
precise: the header for cudaErrorIllegalAddress: "This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched."
source: H1 of F6-05 (CUDA 12.0 headers as installed (Ubuntu package nvidia-cuda-dev 12.0.146~12.0.1-4build4), read in this build: driver_types.h (comments of cudaErrorInvalidConfigu) — installed header read in this build

simple: storing each field in its own array (all x together, all y together) instead of one array of records.
analogy: one shelf of all the salt, one of all the pepper, instead of a box per dish holding one of each.
precise: the layout struct { float x[N], y[N], z[N]; } versus array of structures (AoS) struct { float x, y, z; } p[N]; with SoA, thread t reading x[t] is stride 1.
source: D3 of F6-08 (Wen-mei Hwu, David Kirk, Izzat El Hajj, "Programming Massively Parallel Processors: A Hands-on Approach") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one worker on the GPU doing one small part of the job.
analogy: one kitchen helper.
precise: the smallest unit of execution in CUDA; each thread runs the kernel's code with its own built-in index variables such as threadIdx.  Not an operating-system thread like the std::thread of F2-34: you do not create GPU threads one by one, a launch creates them all.
source: D1 of F6-01 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a thread's seat number at its table, with an x, y and z part.
analogy: seat (3, 5) at a table.
precise: a built-in variable of type uint3 holding the thread's coordinates within its block.
source: D1 of F6-02 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide"); H1 of F6-02 (CUDA 12.0 headers as installed (Ubuntu package nvidia-cuda-dev 12.0.146~12.0.1-4build4), read in this build: vector_types.h (struct dim3: members x, y, z, const) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one instruction that loads several values at once, for example four floats.
analogy: a helper carrying a crate of four jars instead of one jar.
precise: a float4 load compiles to LDG.E.128, a 16-byte load, instead of LDG.E (4 bytes).
source: R4 of F6-09 (load and store instructions of copyScalar and copyVector for target sm_80 (sass_vector.log), CUDA 12.0, compiled only)

simple: the GPU maker's own program that reports the same facts, used as the reference.
analogy: the chain's official sheet for the hall.
precise: for E1, NVIDIA's deviceQuery sample or AMD's rocminfo; nvidia-smi also reports memory and driver.
source: C1 of F6-07 (Systems Curriculum (this project), milestone E1 (build and acceptance test quoted verbatim) and section 13.4. A map, not a source (AH-4))
